hypothesis: A visible split between a human initiation and a machine proposal is co-agency only as a hashed hypothesis. The machine column cannot cross the action boundary. A handoff stays held.

sources.label: Eric Horvitz mixed-initiative framing, restated in Holter, Moruzzi, and El-Assady, Towards agency in human-AI collaboration, IEEE Computer Graphics and Applications, 2026
sources.observation: Mixed-initiative writing treats some interfaces as shared decision surfaces rather than as a tool the person fully drives or an agent that fully acts.
sources.claim: Shared agency means humans and AI co-manage decisions, and agency can be dynamically allocated.
sources.inference: Design material for a local split of initiation and proposal. Not a reason to let a proposal execute, and not a measurement that co-agency occurred.

sources.label: Hector Ouilhet Olmos, The Interface Is Downstream, arXiv:2609.28801, submitted 2026-09-23
sources.observation: The note argues that permissions, evidence rules, and retrieval shape an agent before any reply, and that a retrieved synthesis can be repeated without its chain.
sources.claim: The collaborative interface is upstream of the output: correction and consent have to travel back into what the agent may do.
sources.inference: Void keeps the proposal on the machine side of a held boundary. Retrieved text stays data. It is not an instruction and it is not a seal.

sources.label: Public posts 2106303306641645858, 2105913867587273165, 2105931083577688352, 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-03
sources.observation: In this window a physician account calls a centaur greater than either partner, another post says agency needs veto power, and another says a shared canvas should show intent before side effects.
sources.claim: Man-plus-machine already outperforms either alone, and frictionless agent handoffs can proceed without a person on every step.
sources.inference: The split board can store those claims. It cannot mark them attested, and the handoff control stays disabled.
